We have never stayed in accommodation that was this dirty. The location itself is beautiful, and thankfully, the air conditioning worked.

Only Mimi speaks English; unfortunately, no one else does. Whenever we wanted to order something, we had to use hand gestures and try to explain what we wanted. The food is not recommended either, so we ended up walking to a resort further down the beach to eat.

There were insects everywhere in our room, including biting ants, mosquitoes, and spiders. The bathroom had clumps of hair left behind by previous guests, and judging by the overall condition of the room, it was clear that it had not been properly cleaned.

The water smelled strongly of sewage, which was extremely unpleasant.

The beach loungers are made of bare wood with no cushions, making them very uncomfortable to lie on.

Overall, this place is far too expensive for what you get. The property is in serious need of renovation and, in our opinion, should either be properly renovated or closed until it meets basic standards.

We also did not feel particularly welcomed by the staff. Most of the time, the staff were either sleeping in the hammocks or sitting on their phones. If you decide to stay here, be prepared for very limited English communication and a lack of service.

The location is beautiful, and the air conditioning worked, but unfortunately, those are the only positives we can mention. For the price, we expected much more.

Our stay at Pir Perhentian was unfortunately a great disappointment.
The hotel nevertheless has a real asset: a very beautiful privatized beach, in a beautiful setting.
However, the quality of the room and especially its level of cleanliness are far from what we could expect.
As soon as we arrived, we were confronted with a strong smell of nausea and sewage in the bathroom, which was also far from being clean. The glass was obviously not cleaned and it gave a general impression of lack of maintenance.
The towels provided were also dirty and had yellow spots, which is particularly disappointing and not acceptable for a hotel establishment.
But the most unpleasant thing was to find cockroaches in the room during the night at 4am, one of which appeared on our bedside table as we slept. This kind of situation is particularly stressful and has prevented us from sleeping calmly but from enjoying the full end of our stay. I really didn't feel comfortable in our room at all and didn't take any pleasure in being in it my only desire was to get out of it and a hurry that the stay this ended. We concluded that it was useless to complain at the reception in view of all the previous negative opinions over several years and that nothing had changed or that no refund had been made.

An Amazing Family Getaway at Pulau Perhentian Resort!

We had such a wonderful stay at Pulau Perhentian Resort with our children, and it was truly an unforgettable family holiday! 🏝️💙

The beach was absolutely breathtaking crystal-clear turquoise water, incredibly clean surroundings, and beautiful white sand that sparkles under the sunshine. It felt like a little piece of paradise!

Our room was comfortable, clean and cozy, making it a perfect place to relax after a fun day at the beach. The staff were also very friendly, helpful and welcoming, which made our stay even more enjoyable.

And of course, the food deserves a special mention! 🍽️ Everything we tried was delicious, and we really enjoyed our meals during our stay.

Most importantly, the resort is very family-friendly, and our children had such a great time. Seeing them enjoy the beautiful beach and island made the trip even more special for us.

Thank you Pulau Perhentian Resort for the wonderful hospitality and beautiful memories. We truly enjoyed our stay and would definitely love to come back again! 🌊☀️🤍

Highly recommended for families looking for a relaxing, beautiful and memorable island getaway!

Double feeling about our visit to the Perhentian Islands. Nature is overwhelmingly beautiful. The resort is nicely located in the Turtle bay. The amenities are basically all present at the resort.

However, the quality of the resort is moderate. Cabins are a bit outdated and we had several nights of cockroaches visiting. We stayed 5 nights, not once was the toilet and shower cleaned (we wipe daily cottage, make bed, add new towels and toilet rolls). Staff were moderately helpful with questions and the restaurant was reasonable in quality.

In a jungle hear animals and that with them, monkeys, geckos and squirrels walking around is nice. We enjoyed that.

You can also pay by credit card (at almost all restaurants on the island). Boat service to the other beaches or Kecil can be fast and easy (these do pay in cash). Tip: want to drink wine: Take these from the mainland.

- Room: fair.
- Cleanliness: fair.
- Comfort: fair.
- Location: spectacular.
- Price-quality: expensive.

Spectacular location, but lacking maintenance. The towels are more than an ugly color and everything is old.
As for the service, the staff couldn't be more serious/unfriendly. Only one waitress smiles at you.
As for alcohol, it's forbidden in the restaurant area, and to have a beer you have to go to the resort next door, about 15 minutes away.
What it does have is a spectacular beach, and as soon as you enter you find impressive marine diversity.

Although the place is a little old and could improve the services I would return as this resort is located on the most beautiful beach on the island. In front of the bungalows there is a beautiful beach where you can make snorkling with shark turtles and races. The sunbeds are wooden so I recommend to take a mattress also inflatable to take on land firm because in the island they do not sell. You eat well à la carte instead the buffet leaves a little to want. Food prices are good compared to Italy. We spent at dinner about 10 euros per head. Cleanliness leaves a bit to be desired but just do it present and come to re clean. The Personal with us was available. I traveled with friends and my two-year-old son and I'd be back despite everything. The position is priceless.

I want to be fair. Perhaps this would have been a wonderful experience for a young family, if they are OK with very “rustic” accommodations. We are not that young family. We paid $800 ringgit per night for what we believed would be at least an adequate resort (in Kuala Lumpur, that same $800 would have more than paid for a suite in a 5-star hotel). Our expectations were not super high, since we understood that we were paying for an experience on a private island. Just clean and comfortable. Unfortunately, we got neither. Our room, #208 had a broken front door that only opened 1/3 of the way, scraping across the floor and then stopping. There were deep gouges and white paint all over the floor, which let us know this issue is ongoing. At first glance, the room looked clean (and bedding was fresh), but on further inspection we could see that only surface cleaning has ever been done. The doors were filthy, mold stains on walls, absolute filth in the pipes and shower drain and air conditioning filters. Dirty, streaked mirrors. Also, the king size bed was hard as a rock - extremely uncomfortable with a poor quality mattress. We paid an extra $100 ringgit for an “extra bed” which was just a cot - a plastic mattress. Food at PIR is bad and obscenely expensive. Piles of trash behind convenience stores and coffee shops. And overall, a deeply unpleasant sewage smell in our room and permeating the island. The good: beach is absolutely lovely. Water is crystal clear, sand is white. No trash on the beach (they hide trash behind businesses, but it’s obvious as it stinks and attracts rodents). It was a wonderful experience to swim with colorful tropical fish. That was the one and only thing I appreciated about this overpriced and horrifically maintained island.

The location is very nice but the resort is extremely neglected and swollen. Bedline stained, moulded bathroom with yellow water out of the tap, insects, dust on the conditioner and never clean bathroom (consign new toilet paper and emptying basket only for explicit request) with few towels. Very uncomfortable wooden slopes and common places not properly maintained and in some cases abandoned seeds. It is a shame because the jungle and the sea are extremely lively and full of animals but the resort is not recommended. Better to come by boat and stay in another hotel.

The location is nice, but unfortunately the room was pretty bad and definitely not what we expected. Very basic, dated and extremely overpriced for what you get. Definitely needs some serious improvements.

Beautiful resort with great potential, but service needs improvement – 7.5/10||We spent a week at this Marriott resort and overall had a very enjoyable stay. The property is beautiful, our accommodation was extremely comfortable, the views were wonderful, and we really appreciated our  villa with a private pool.||Breakfast was definitely one of the highlights — excellent variety and quality, especially the freshly! |A special mention must go to Zafirah, our Villa Host, who was absolutely wonderful: kind, attentive, always available and genuinely interested in making our stay special. We also really appreciated the lovely touches for our wedding anniversary.||That said, for a 5-star Marriott resort at this price level, there are some areas that really need improvement.||The biggest issue for us was the restaurant service. Although the staff were always friendly, service was consistently very slow and dishes for the same table rarely arrived together. On several occasions, one of us had almost finished eating before the other person’s meal arrived.|There were also some surprising operational issues. The beach bar was out of basic items, including water, for several days, which is difficult to understand at a 5-star tropical resort.||The management of sunbeds around the pool also needs attention. Guests reserve them early with towels and belongings and sometimes do not appear until hours later. We were told there is a 15–20 minute policy for unattended sunbeds, but unfortunately we never saw it being enforced.||Finally, the arrival experience could be much more polished. First impressions matter, and the transfer/check-in process did not feel particularly premium or aligned with what we expected from a resort of this category.||Overall, we would rate our experience 7.5/10. There is a lot to love here: beautiful surroundings, excellent accommodation, a great breakfast and some genuinely lovely staff. However, at this price point, the consistency of the service needs to match the quality of the resort itself.||With better restaurant coordination, attention to basic stock management, enforcement of pool policies and a more refined arrival experience, this could very easily become a 9/10 resort.

What a waste while the potential is there and the site is beautiful!
The rooms: overall dirty, the dilapidated bathroom, the cleaning (vu) is made (in 5') with a beach towel without cleaning products (this explains this), broken or unmaintained equipment. The surroundings are dirty and ns finally picked up what was hanging around the room.
Food: go eat in the hotel next door! The bins are not filled continuously, it must count 30'. We paid a buffet (×3) and there was only one tray of rice and one tray of meat, the other 10 were empty at 7:30 p.m. At the end of 40' we left, the stomach almost empty... the environment is also dirty and not engaging.

The wise management apologized and sent a team to make a complete cleanup. That's nice, but the other days: back to habits.

All this spoiled our stay (4days) which was saved by the restaurant next door and by the magnificent underwater bottoms.

It's a shame because the site has potential, it's just missing a real hotel management: check the quality of the house, keep the dining area clean, rework the buffet continuously and check the surroundings of the site to remove the waste that is in its midst.

I'm very, very, very, very mixed at this hotel.

The beach is terribly beautiful and the hotel is terribly old. I've moved from being sleek to disgust throughout my stay.

The first certainty is that when you stay there, you have to be very comfortable with wildlife: jeckos, lizards, ants, locusts, squirrels that look like rats, varans and even Malay varans. In the room, there is still a warning against all this wildlife and also against snakes. Honestly, we haven't seen one. But all these animals are omnipresent. So I spent a stay in a state of maximum alert,

Then, the room is dirty as possible, it smells of sewers and bed linen and bath linen is... pitiful. Holed, stained, yellow... I have put pictures but the general unsanitaryness of the hotel is indescribable. Beach deckchairs are wooden boards without mattresses and there are no umbrellas. If you put yourself under the palm trees, beware of the squirrels who have terrified some of them.
Finally, breakfast is very short, the undefinable coffee: oil black but absolutely no taste of coffee. The evening restaurant was truly right. There is nothing to do at night, plan an IPad and a 4/5G connection that works very well. There's no wifi.

As for the beach... Wow! Perhentian's most beautiful. We swam daily with rays, turtles, baby sharks etc.

There are plenty of people coming to the day (it's the boat parade though) And I wonder if that's not what we really have to do. Anyway.

So I wouldn't advise to go there because of the magic of the beach but to go there knowingly and paying the right price because I paid on Agoda/Booking more than 300€ at night and at that price, it's a genuine flight.

We stayed here for two nights with my husband to celebrate our wedding anniversary, and everything was absolutely perfect! The location is incredible, with a private beach that is among the most beautiful I have seen in Malaysia (and honestly… anywhere else too). The staff were incredibly kind, welcoming and always happy to help. Our room was wonderful, with a breathtaking view. The package also included several activities that we really enjoyed, such as snorkeling with turtles and kayaking. We were also incredibly lucky to take part in a turtle hatchling release, supporting SEATRUE, an organization dedicated to protecting these beautiful animals. It was a truly emotional and unforgettable experience. The food at the restaurant was also very good, and breakfast was excellent and plentiful.
There is also the opportunity to join yoga classes, either on the beach in the morning or in the dedicated yoga space overlooking the sea. Our instructor, Huril, was incredibly kind and very knowledgeable. The classes were both relaxing and enjoyable, but also challenging in the best possible way! I highly recommend staying at this resort and truly hope to be able to come back in the future!

Beautiful  resort made better by excellent service. Especially good service from Guest Ambassador Saiful - very attentive with the food recommendations and preparations. Accommodating to our request for traditional food.

Really good breakfast.

All the staff were extremely kind—Nadia at the reception in particular was super helpful and friendly.|​Dining: Several restaurants on-site; the Asian one was really good.|​Beach & Sea: Beautiful beach and crystal-clear water, with a spot for turtle watching right nearby.|​Services: Super efficient shuttle service and everything was perfectly organized.

What a waste.... such a nice site as poorly managed...!!Yes, the site is splendid and the architecture of the hotel has potential but it is not managed at all:!1) the rooms: are generally dirty and some of the equipment dilapidated: broken bathroom furniture, bezel of the wanking toilets, unspeakable shower hose, dirty shower glass2) cleaning: jai attended the house which was made with a beach towel without any product in 5' chrono (no broom or nothing). Re-scaling is random and often wait +30' before seeing the re-filled bins. So we paid for a buffet and on the 10th of the trays only 3 were filled, they were more than 30' later, when we left (the hollow belly). Same morning and noon. The solution: go and eat in the hotel next to (10' on foot) where the service is smiling and the card attractive. We had all our meals. The management, warned of our remarks, apologized and sent a cleaning team to make our room (white) it is nice and commercial but the problem is not there. It is in the non-existent controls: no one to check the cleanliness of the rooms, of the site (we ended up cleaning around our room the scattered waste) , of the dining area. This spoiled our stay that was saved by the restaurant next door and the magnificent submarine bottoms.

This hotel is a disaster. Service, cleaning, food, nothing's right. Only the location is ideal, by the sea. Small sharks, rays and fish can be seen by the water.
My advice: look for the hotels next door.

The hotel is very well located on one of the best beaches. However, for what you pay it's very expensive — they give you torn, worn-out towels, room cleaning is basically nonexistent, they just sweep a little and that's it. Above all, if you go, don't look in the corners of the rooms. It's disgusting.

Recommended for 2-3 nights but not more.

Great location, right on the beach. Pretty room and clean enough though there is a slightly unpleasant smell in the bathroom and has never been cleaned during the stay. The resort complex and rooms should be freshened and cleaned better.
The wifi does not work and there is no TV in the room. The restaurant is nothing.
With some adjustment, cleanliness, and improvements it would have a high potential.
It's an amazing neighborhood. Beach and place for snorkeling. The hotel itself has a lot to improve. Very weak Internet. Bad breakfast and expensive restaurant.

Beautiful island.
We were a little against our stay, considering all the negative reviews. But the room was clean (bathroom somewhat outdated). Pool is neat, beach is nice. Snack bar also fine for lunch. Staff was very friendly and helpful to us. In short, it wasn't so bad! Bed was covered every day, clean towels and 2 bottles of water every day. We did food every night at Barat, there with 19s always good food.

Recommended: jungle trekking to other side island. Starting point is badminton field.

The beach is stunning! White sand, turquoise sea and turtles and sharks 5 meters away from the coast. The beach front bungalows have an amazing view and location. The accommodation is clean, but very basic, old and worn. The bed is comfortable and the air conditioning works. The resorts itself is very tired, breakfast was so poor I stopped going, and the staff look exhausted and totally fed up. If your priority is beach life and you are happy to explore other food options, and a simple room and bathroom are ok for you then this resort could work for you!

We spent at this resort 5 days and 4 nights. To begin I must say that we have dreamed of the Perenthian Islands for months, and I must say that they do not disappoint expectations, they are an unspoilt paradise! But we started a bit discouraged by the reviews of the various structures and after a research year we agreed to book at the PIR room beach front. Chapter location: definitely the most beautiful beach of both islands, the beach is located in Besar(large island), excellent location, turtle point 50 m from the shore. Every day we bathed in the midst of fishes of every species, races and many shark black fins who came regularly to visit us, wonderful feeling! Room Chapter: the beach front room is definitely the best of the resort, we chose the breakfast package included, the room is wooden, definitely not luxury but I would say the 3 star cheques. However it has this seafront balcony, every morning we woke up with the noise of the sea practically 30 seconds away from us. Clean room, of course you have to keep in mind that you are on a fairly wild island in Malaysia. Chapter services; the boys working at the PIR are all very kind and friendly, surely I would put more beds on the beach and maybe a more comfortable type, but what do you make of the sunbeds when you have that heavenly sand? Food Chapter: PIR breakfast was quite provided with a good international and especially Asian choice. Conclusions: our summer experience more than positive! Obviously you have to take into account that you are on a wild island, with a dream sea that definitely has nothing to envy to places like the Maldives. Needless to look for a 5 star service, here you come to be detached from the world! I highly recommend it to those who want to immerse themselves in this paradise.

Resort staff are hospitality and friendly to welcome us at the resort’s lobby, the room is equipped with all amenities needed and we have a big room with the living room separated. Beach is wonderful with the white sand and crystal clear water. I like the beach bench under the small hut to feels the peace and calmness.

We had a wonderful honeymoon at the Taaras Beach & Spa Resort. The location could not be better. Wonderful private beach, crystal clear water, fine sand and a very intimate feeling. The service was exceptional. The whole staff made us feel very privileged.

Honestly if you're thinking about it, just book it! Such a beautiful hotel, amazing views, great food and brilliant staff. Everyone was so friendly and helpful, Especially Hamdan, he was always checking in to make sure we was ok and if there was anything we needed. Thanks again for a brilliant stay. I will be back!

Magnificent experience, spectacular island with excellent hospitality. The Resort is a bit dated but offers that familiarity that is often lost in new structures. Beautiful philosophy behind the preservation of the island.

The taaras is located in a lovely bay, crystal clear water and white sand where it is easy to meet colorful turtle fish and small harmless sharks. For the rest the structure is beautiful but in my opinion not up to a 5 stars. The kitchen is wide, but not as international as they say. flavors are mainly Asian. The staff is very friendly and kind, the wooden bungalows are very beautiful. Among the various activities organize the excursions in front of the beach, which sincerely are easily accessible independently with a canoe at no cost. In the evening there is not much movement, a bit of live music that ends soon. Overall a beautiful place that however pays and not little.

I spent a week in this earthly paradise and left my heart really. We start with the main aspect of the structure: POSITION! The PIR, believe me, lies on the most beautiful beach of the Perhentians! Coral sand, blinding! A sea, I confirm that nothing has to envy in the Maldives! If you come here you do not need excursions! The sea in front of you will give you snorkelling exits to see turtles, shark black fins, gray coats, clown fish...and, if you are particularly lucky as I was, the Napoleon fish!
Breakfast is Asian and western with an egg station. I recommend that you consider it. The restaurant is very slow. I have always taken rice or meat: we Italians are a little complicated! There is no possibility of alcohol! If you are in abstinence go to the neighbors: at the PIR no chance. The rooms are comfortable and spacious. AC works well. Cleaning is scarce and there is hot water... but it was never a problem! WiFi only works at the reception and bad: if you need to upgrade the OS or large GB go early in the morning and/or late in the evening...
Of course... a little suitcase with you you must carry it but this sea will reward you with interests!
Redang board excursions: it is yes the most expensive but Redang is worth believing me!
Kecil: go one night to his twin on long beach. Sit on one of the many locals and choose the fish you want to eat. Then go see the fire show!

I miss you!!! !

Dirty room (telecde climat covered with finger marks, greyish sheets and badly smelling dito user towels, one can no longer see through the dressing glass of the shower, blattes in the shower, cutting down unstable toilet, rat seen on the frameworks of the dining space, restaurant not terrible at all, personal more interested by their smartphone than by their job, space to potential but not maintenance. The beach is good and the sea is warm and turquoise but pass your way.

Incredible potential - very disappointing execution. If I start with the positives, the resort is situated on an incredible beach, crystal clear sea with a simple water taxi system that can take you to a number of other beautiful locations around the island. The resort itself would be best described as neglected. Full of promise and really disappointing delivery as the rooms are less than clean, with very dated bathrooms and evidence of bed bugs that had once infested the room. The rooms are very close to the beach, making the views from the balcony a bit of a bonus. The facilities in the resort were pretty rubbish to be honest, a dirty unused pool, empty games room, one set of badminton rackets for the entire hotel to share, a karaoke room that you can pay extra to use, absolutely no daytime/evening entertainment and breakfast/dinner service that was quite shocking. I wouldn’t mind having limited service but the resort advertises WiFi, then informs you on arrival that it is only available in reception - a place you probably want to avoid as much as possible. One of the reasons to travel to SE Asia is for the food, then you are met with a cold, stale selection of buffet food. The BBQ buffet somehow doubles the price of the service whilst serving much of the same food but warmed on the grill before service. I think the lowlight of the resort however has to be the service from the reception team. The ladies appeared frankly irritated during any interaction and would best be described as less than welcoming. The laundry service was not running due to “bad water”, despite it being promoted on the room information - not sure if this was a short term or long term issue they were having.

I was unfortunate enough to suffer from a series of lacerations on my hand from a quite bizarre needlefish attack, this led to significant bleeding. The receptionists were completely uninterested in helping me, nor did they demonstrate any empathy as I bled out in reception. I was lucky enough that a paramedic guest was checking in at that time and assisted me. Bizarrely, the receptionists weren’t even enthusiastic about having the blood cleaned from the floor and it dried/remained there for the final day of our stay. Their service peaked when they asked us to return the spare roll of toilet paper that we had been using to help clean up some of the spilled blood - there is no telling what they would have wanted to do with it had we obliged, which we did not.

We stayed for three nights as a family of four and appreciated being upgraded to a larger two-bedroom Cliff Bay Suite. It was spacious and comfortable, and the complimentary minibar on arrival was a nice touch.

The resort’s greatest strength is undoubtedly its setting: a truly beautiful beach, clear water and a sheltered bay. Snorkelling with turtles was one of the highlights of our stay. We also paid to visit the turtle conservation centre, where our children learned about conservation and, under close supervision, carefully helped uncover baby turtles from the sand. It was a meaningful and memorable experience.

The complimentary entertainment lounge—with foosball, pool, table tennis, mahjong and carrom—was another good feature for families. Some staff were genuinely warm, friendly and full of smiles, particularly at ASEAN All Day Dining. The breakfast buffet itself, however, had a surprisingly limited spread for a five-star resort.

Unfortunately, service elsewhere was inconsistent. Some buggy drivers appeared uninterested, and we observed one using his phone while driving, which was a genuine safety concern. Drinks ordered from the bar never arrived, while indoor dining involved long waits and follow-up calls. The repeated lapses across different departments suggested wider issues with training, supervision and internal communication rather than a single isolated incident.

Food and drinks were expensive, yet the quality and service did not consistently justify the prices. The excursions were also costly, although the turtle conservation visit was a worthwhile exception. The kids’ club felt basic and underwhelming for a family resort at this price point. While our upgraded suite was spacious, the room and several other areas felt dated and overdue for refurbishment.

We also found it odd that sustainability videos from 2020 were still being shown without more recent updates. Our conservation-centre visit showed that at least some valuable work continues, but relying on six-year-old material leaves guests wondering about the progress of the resort’s other initiatives. The beach and water remain beautiful, although they did not always appear quite as pristine as in the older footage.

The Taaras has the ingredients to be exceptional: an extraordinary beach, memorable wildlife experiences, spacious accommodation and clear international appeal, including among the many Italian visitors we encountered. However, a five-star experience must also include consistently attentive service, safe practices, well-maintained facilities, good food and value for money. On those measures, our stay felt closer to a four-star experience despite luxury-level prices.

As Malaysian guests, we genuinely wanted to support and recommend a local resort attracting visitors from around the world. That is why this was more disappointing than upsetting. With better training, coordination, maintenance and value, The Taaras could be outstanding. Based on our experience and the price paid, however, we would find it difficult to recommend it in its present form.

Perhentian Island Resort sits on what is arguably the most breathtaking, crystal-clear stretch of white sand and turtle-snorkeling reef on the entire island. However, the resort itself is a massive letdown. You are paying a premium price for a property that feels neglected, dated, and poorly managed.

The Bad: The rooms are in desperate need of a renovation—expect septic tank smell from poorly maintained toilets, musty smell, stained linens, plumbing issues, in room safe that does not work , and zero Wi-Fi or poor phone signal in the chalets. - we changed rooms and had the same issues. The included buffet breakfast is incredibly basic and lacks quality and cleanliness (flies on food) while the overall resort infrastructure struggled with basic utilities like running water. (We could not shower, flush, or wash hands at one point our stay). 2 rooms per chalet have very thin walls, so expect smelling and hearing your neighbour if they have a conversation, or smoke a cigarette.

The Good: The location is a 10/10. The water is pristine, and you can literally swim out from the shore to snorkel with sea turtles and fish without needing a boat tour.

Final Thoughts and recommendations: Do not look at the booking photos; they do not reflect the current run-down state of the rooms and common areas. Save yourself the frustration: book a better-maintained hotel nearby for a comfortable night's sleep, and just take a water taxi over to this beach during the day to enjoy the spectacular nature.

Recommend to upgrade at least on plumbing and ventilation infrastructures, and management to have goals to realise the full potential of this wonderful location.

For our recent getaway, we booked The Taaras, supposedly the best hotel on Redang Island. With that reputation and the price tag, we arrived expecting a little bit of wow.

Arrival:
The welcome was pretty much “hey you made it.”  . We were served a welcome drink that tasted as if the juice concentrate was more of a suggestion than an ingredient.

We arrived way too early and our room wasn’t ready for early check-in, so we were then told to leave our bags on the floor by the stairs. For a resort charging these rates, I assumed a proper luggage area might have made it into the budget, but apparently not- the staircase floor is the luggage lounge.

We left our bags to enjoy the beach, and we can confirm this is where The Taaras absolutely earns its reputation.

The beach:
The beach is breathtaking. Hands down, the most beautiful beach on Redang Island. The sand is incredibly white, the water is crystal clear, and the scenery is spectacular. If the welcome drink was 99% water and 1% juice, at least the water at the beach was actually impressive.

The room:
Our Bay View room was amazing. A big thank you to the hotel management for assigning us Room 251. The room was perfect, and the view of the beach was spectacular. We loved the slice of cake and the beautiful anniversary message displayed on the screen- though we had to turn on the TV to see it. It was a thoughtful touch.

Breakfast at Asian Dining restaurant:
Breakfast had a good spread, although most of the food sat comfortably in the moderately good category. The croissant was soft, and limp. The roti canai was fine, even though i think a splash of sambal would take it up a notch.

We ordered iced chocolate drinks, which arrived as a joke. Between this and the welcome drink, I strongly suspect the beverage department is either terrified of flavour or operating under extremely strict flavor rationing. Perhaps a little more training in beverage making?

Recreation Center:
We made good use of the Sports and Recreation Center. Renting equipment such as the canoes, snorkelling gear and an underwater camera was easy, and returning everything was straightforward. The staff were extremely helpful, especially Kak Husni, who made things simple for us

The only issue though was transferring the underwater camera files. We couldn’t transfer everything because the videos were large, despite averaging around two minutes each. If only the centre could temporarily upload the files to cloud storage and provide guests with a download link. That would save everyone from standing around watching a transfer progress bar move with the urgency of a sea cucumber.

Customer Service:
One thing that genuinely stood out was the customer service. The staff were consistently friendly and helpful, when approached, but some moments went beyond the usual resort service. A staff member helped attend to our minor wounds after a snorkelling activity, and we even saw another staff member helping a guest tie her hair. How lovely is that.

We had the pleasure of riding with Rafiq, one of the buggy drivers, who remembered us by our room number, so every trip between our room and the lobby was effortless. He shared helpful tips and was a pleasure to chat with.

Overall, The Taaras has an absolutely spectacular beach, beautiful views, excellent rooms and some genuinely wonderful staff. The natural setting does a lot of the heavy lifting.

They just have to work on the arrival experience, and beverage quality.

I also found it very convenient to have the village right next to the resort, where you can dine in local restaurants spending about a third compared to hotel restaurants and, often, eating even better.

The mattress is very comfortable, in the common room there are games to entertain and the weather was perfect: despite the forecasts indicated continuous rain, we had only short night showers. The sea is simply the warmest and most blue I have ever seen and during the stay you can observe many marine animals.

There are also some improvements. Sand mosquitoes are numerous, even within the rooms: I recommend to bring a really effective repellent. Some deck chairs and tables on the beach would need more accurate cleaning.

I did not appreciate the constant presence of the owner's yacht anchored in the bay, because it spoils a bit the natural view of this magnificent place.

The most sad note concerns unfortunately the amount of plastic and microplastics present both on the beach and at sea. The owner proudly shows the projects of requalification and cleaning, an admirable initiative, but unfortunately it is enough to make a few steps to find microplastics, bottles, lighters and other waste. I would have liked to find baskets or bags made available to guests who want to spend some of their time cleaning up this paradise.

Finally, I would enjoy a little more evening entertainment. Apart from the pleasant live music, the evenings are quite quiet: a disco evening, a white party or some additional show would make the experience even more complete.

Overall I recommend The Taaras Beach & Spa to those looking for the most beautiful sea you can imagine, a well-managed resort and a very attentive service. With some improvement and a more balanced price-quality ratio could really become an absolute point of reference.

We stayed at The Taaras hoping for a relaxing family getaway, and while parts of it delivered, several avoidable issues took the shine off.

Room allocation: Before arriving, we specifically requested twin rooms in the same block, ideally close to reception, and were told this would be "accommodated." Despite the resort not being at full occupancy, we were placed in the garden view block furthest from reception — not the twins-together setup we'd asked for. Not the start we were hoping for.

Check-in: The check-in process itself felt underwhelming and rushed. We weren't given any orientation — no signage or directions to the beach, and no mention of the sandfly issue (more on that below) or the turtle release happening that same evening. We only found out about the turtle release from friendly staff down at the beach, and it ended up being a real highlight — but it shouldn't have been left to chance. It should also have been mentioned during check in that the hot water only works if you turn on the SWITCH for 15 minutes before taking a shower . as a result a poor cold first day shower experience with poor water pressure

Sandflies: This was our biggest issue. Nobody warned us about sandflies, and by the end of day one I'd been bitten around 25 times and my son closer to 50. The itching kept us both up most of the night. A simple heads-up at check-in (with repellent recommendations, or even repellent provided) would have made a huge difference.

Wifi: In-room wifi was patchy and unreliable throughout our stay.
The positives: The rooms themselves were genuinely luxurious and matched the price point. The beach is stunning — genuinely one of the best we've experienced — and the turtle release was a magical, unexpected bonus.

Spa: A real highlight of the trip. Glory's team massage was fantastic, and the traditional Taaras herbal bag massage was excellent — worth booking in advance. Glory herself was the first person we met who we could say embodied a true 5 star experience!

Staff: Mixed experience. The beach staff and spa team were warm and attentive. Reception, however, could use more training in guest service — better attention to pre-arrival requests and basic welcome information would go a long way, including information (and a basic leaflet for asking us to check amentiies via scannign a QR code - available we found AFTERWARDS)

In summary: Gorgeous location, excellent spa, but the resort needs to tighten up communication — from honoring room requests to warning guests about sandflies and letting them know about evening events like the turtle release.

There were also quite a lot of ants in the room, as well as several issues with the finishing that, in our opinion, do not fit a hotel presenting itself as a luxury golf resort. The door was sticking when both opening and closing. The wooden bathroom door showed clear signs of wood rot and had been poorly repaired. Since there is no shower curtain, the door gets very wet after every shower, which certainly does not help. The sealant around the sink also looked very old and overdue for replacement.

The dining experience also felt rather dated. The menus at the restaurant and bars are old-fashioned laminated, folded A4 sheets, and several items listed on them were simply not available, including drinks such as Hoegaarden, Corona and Piña Colada. There is also very little communication about which restaurants and bars are open and when. For a resort of this size and standard, we would expect both the menus and the communication about the available dining options to be kept more up to date.

We also found that quite a lot of staff members were travelling back and forth around the resort on scooters. Given the size of the property, this is perhaps understandable, but it does take away somewhat from the peaceful resort atmosphere you might expect from a place like this.

Berjaya Tioman Resort proudly presents itself as the largest resort on Tioman. We are aware that the resort is currently undergoing renovations and that some room categories have already been updated. However, this does not fully address the issue from a guest's perspective. At present, it seems to be a matter of luck whether you receive a renovated room or one that is clearly in need of updating, while paying the same price. Until the renovation is completed across the resort, the experience can therefore vary considerably depending on the room you are allocated.

In our view, the remaining rooms should be brought up to current standards, with more consistency across the resort in terms of both room quality and overall presentation.

Fortunately, there are also positive aspects. The activities on offer are well organised, and the lobby staff are incredibly friendly, helpful and accommodating. When we arrived, we were initially given a room with two single beds, even though we had booked a double bed. After we raised this, it was resolved quickly and without any hassle.

In short: a beautifully located resort with friendly staff and well-organised activities, but the condition of some of the rooms and the dated overall presentation unfortunately seriously detract from the overall experience. A thorough renovation and update would certainly be worthwhile.

At high tide, the water can cover much of the island and you can have beautiful clear water directly underneath your chalet. At low tide, the water recedes, there may be little or no water beneath the chalet, and the exposed sand makes the island appear much larger. It was really interesting to watch the landscape transform with the tides.

Kapalai is a very special place and a fantastic choice for anyone who loves diving, marine life, and staying somewhere completely different from a typical resort. It's definitely worth the travel from Tawau airport. We would definitely recommend it!

An exceptional setting that deserves an experience to the height...

We stayed at Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort for our honeymoon, and the place is simply amazing. The hotel is beautiful, perfectly integrated with its surroundings, with typical rooms full of charm.
We had a coral-side room, which we highly recommend: the ocean view is exceptional and, in the evening, the turtles come literally to say good night to you.
The location is absolutely superb.

Underwater, there are a lot of things to see, including very large turtles, and in quantity! It is a real pleasure to see them evolve in their natural environment.
On the other hand, we should not come here expecting to discover an immense intact coral barrier. However, marine wealth remains very interesting and encounters with turtles are definitely worth a visit.

The points that disappointed us...
Unfortunately, the main negative point concerns some of the clientele, particularly Chinese tourist groups. Their behaviour has sometimes really spoiled the charm and tranquillity of the place: shouting, disrespect for staff and other customers, and behaviors that seemed unsuited to an establishment of this standing.
We also felt that the organization of the resort was very focused on this clientele.
It is a shame, because such an exceptional setting would deserve a much more calm and respectful atmosphere.
In particular, we find it unfortunate that the hotel reserves a large part of its rooms directly to Chinese agencies. This seems to contribute to a strong concentration of this clientele in the resort and, consequently, to the sometimes very noisy and unrespectful atmosphere that we saw during our stay.

The buffet, another point to improve...
We know that we are in an all-inclusive 3-star resort and we obviously did not expect gastronomy. But with simple products, it would be quite possible to offer a much more qualitative cuisine.
We found many industrial products, which is a pity, and relatively few Malaysian specialties. This is particularly regrettable when one comes from abroad and wants to discover the local cuisine. Again, we sometimes felt that the buffet was more suited to Chinese customer habits than to an international clientele.

In summary:
The Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort could really have everything a 4-star hotel thanks to its exceptional setting, charming rooms, unique location, staff quality and especially its excellent diving center.
Unfortunately, there are some choices about the welcome and the restaurant that we feel are ruining some of the experience and preventing the establishment from being fully up to its exceptional environment.
Nevertheless, this remains a beautiful place and particularly suitable for a honeymoon. Sleeping in the middle of the ocean, waking up with this view and seeing the turtles passing in front of his room is an experience that we will not forget
This is where I and my family dream, and where there are family favorites and turtles that see more than they can imagine.

Before getting to the Taaras, we had heard so many great things about the place. Even ChatGPT says it’s considered *the country’s* highest end hotel. We thought that was the reason why we were asked to pay 400€ per night (2 people room). If you have never traveled to Malaysia, you might not be aware of the currency value, so just know that an average meal for 2 is worth 100MYR (20€). Therefore you can only imagine how expensive this hotel is. Now, for this kind of money you really do expect the best of the best. Unfortunately, as you might have guessed already, that’s not the case. This was quite literally the worst hotel we’ve stayed at since we landed in Malaysia. Besides the staff being very kind, although most of the times you feel the service doesn’t reach the luxury they promise, and the private beach being objectively beautiful, the rest is honestly terrible. The rooms are big, yes, but super dark and old - in fact, the furniture must have stayed the same since the resort opened in 1996. 2 out of the 3 restaurants available in the resort are quite bad both aesthetically and food wise. The Italian/Indian one is ok, but we spent 450MYR (90€) for 2 mains and 1 plate of fruit, so also not great. The pool is always dirty and infested by kids. The resort also offers “complimentary” activities - too bad we wanted to rent gear for SUP and they answered it was already taken - wasn’t aware 5 star hotels only owned 1 paddle surf. We also spent 180MYR (40€) for a snorkeling activity, which was basically right beside the beach, so we could have just swum to the snorkeling location, and without the other 15 people that were with us. As mentioned, the beach is really nice, white sands, pristine water - all great. Too bad the sun beds are as decadent as the rest of the resort, plus there’s a big unbalance between the number of beds and the amount of guests the complex can host. Overall, a terrible experience very much misaligned with the price you pay.

🎯 Facilities & Overall Experience

One area for improvement would be the swimming pool, which is relatively small and looks a bit dated. However, this was not a major drawback for us since the beach is just nearby and serves as a better alternative. The pool feels more like a complementary feature rather than the main attraction.

✅ Overall
A great resort for a relaxing family getaway, with excellent service, kid-friendly facilities, and a beautiful private beachfront — with some minor room and facility improvements that could further enhance the experience.

I recently spent 3 nights at Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort, and unfortunately, it was a major disappointment. While the location is naturally beautiful, the resort’s management and operations are overwhelmingly biased toward a specific demographic, leaving international travelers in the dark and ignoring basic environmental ethics.
Communication & Service Gaps
The resort feels entirely geared toward mainland Chinese tourists, to the point where English-speaking guests are treated as an afterthought.
• The Briefing: Our "welcome briefing" in English lasted a mere 2 minutes and lacked vital information. Meanwhile, the Chinese-language briefing went on for 20 minutes. We missed out on key details, such as the option to visit neighboring islands to purchase fresh seafood to bring back.
• Logistics: Announcements are a struggle. When calling room numbers for boat departures or activities, staff used Chinese numbers only. Despite my name being clearly English on the manifest, I had to guess when they were referring to me.
• Payments: Even the bar is restrictive. They  accept QR code payments designed for mainland Chinese users, no acceptance of international credit cards or cash.
Environmental & Diving Concerns
This was the most upsetting part of the stay. For a resort located in such a delicate marine ecosystem, the lack of oversight is appalling.
• Wildlife Harassment: I witnessed guests (specifically from the majority group) petting and harassing sea turtles. Despite reporting this to the staff multiple times, zero action was taken.
• Poor Diving Standards: Many of the divers currently visiting appear to be unqualified or poorly trained. I saw constant reef damage—divers kicking the coral, touching marine life, and poking animals for photos.
• Staff Negligence: The dive guides and resort staff seem to prioritize guest "satisfaction" (allowing them to do whatever they want) over the protection of the reef.
Final Verdict
If you are an English speaker or a diver who cares about marine conservation and reef etiquette, stay elsewhere. The blatant disregard for environmental rules and the massive language barrier in service makes this resort a poor choice for global travelers. There are far better options in the Semporna area that respect both their guests and the ocean.

Staying at Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort truly felt like disconnecting from everyday life. The resort is built over the sea, surrounded by water in every direction, with a very peaceful atmosphere. Sunrises and sunsets are beautiful, and at night you only hear the sound of the ocean — perfect for relaxing and relieving stress.

Diving is definitely the highlight. The nearby dive sites around Kapalai are rich in macro marine life, and the dive guides are professional and patient, always taking time to point out small creatures. Even for non-expert divers, the experience feels safe and enjoyable. The schedule is well-paced and not rushed.

The water villas are simple but comfortable, clean, with good air conditioning and comfortable beds. WiFi is limited, but that actually helps you unplug and fully relax.

Food options are not extensive, but meals are fresh and satisfying, especially after diving.
Overall, this is not a resort for nightlife or entertainment, but if you come for diving and true relaxation, Sipadan Kapalai is absolutely worth it.

Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort was truly one of the most unforgettable travel experiences of my life. If you love the ocean, nature, and marine life, this place is an absolute dream come true. Everything about the resort — from the location to the scenery to the water activities — feels like a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

The moment you arrive, you’ll be amazed by how beautiful Kapalai is. The waters are unbelievably clear, with stunning shades of blue and turquoise that you usually only see in photos. The resort sits on stilts above the sea, and the whole environment feels peaceful, private, and close to nature. Waking up to the sound of the ocean and seeing the sunrise over the water is something I will never forget.

What made this trip extra special for me is that I managed to snorkel and dive for the first time here. It was such a memorable and exciting experience! I was a bit nervous at the beginning, but the team guided me well and made me feel safe and confident. Snorkeling in Kapalai was already amazing — the visibility is so clear that you can see colourful fish, coral, and marine life easily, even near the resort area. It felt like entering a totally different world under the sea.

And the diving experience… wow. It was truly breathtaking. For a first-timer, this was the perfect place because the water is calm, crystal clear, and filled with marine life. I felt so excited and amazed seeing the underwater scenery up close — it’s something you cannot describe fully with words. It’s one of those experiences that stays with you forever.

The resort itself is also very comfortable and well managed. The rooms are clean, cosy, and relaxing, and the overall atmosphere is calm and peaceful — perfect for a full getaway from busy city life. The staff are friendly, professional, and helpful, and they really make you feel taken care of. Meals were enjoyable as well, and it’s nice to dine while enjoying the beautiful sea view around you.

Overall, Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort is a place I would highly recommend to anyone. Even if you’ve never snorkeled or dived before (like me), this is the perfect location to try — it’s safe, exciting, and absolutely unforgettable. The clear waters, stunning marine life, and peaceful environment make it a must-visit. Definitely one of the best and most memorable trips I’ve ever had, and I would love to come back again!

We spent our anniversary at The Taaras Beach & Spa Resort and had an amazing experience overall. This was already our fifth stay at this beautiful resort, which says a lot about how much we enjoy this special place.

The location is truly a gem — the bay is stunning, the beach remains one of the most beautiful in Malaysia, and the staff are exceptionally friendly and welcoming. We will definitely return again.

That said, there are a few areas that deserve attention and improvement.

The general condition of the resort shows signs of aging and a major renovation is becoming necessary. The old roofing with visible discoloration gives parts of the resort an outdated feeling. The pool area also needs refurbishment, especially the bridge near the pool, which looks worn and old. A general revamp would greatly elevate the overall luxury experience.

The location alone cannot guarantee long-term success if maintenance and modernization are not prioritized. Considering the room rates range between RM2,500 and RM4,500 per night — making Taaras one of the most expensive resorts in Malaysia — guest expectations are naturally very high.

For these prices, I expected more attention to detail, especially regarding food and beverage quality. Breakfast should include genuinely fresh-squeezed orange juice, not artificial juice labeled as “fresh.” Small upgrades can make a huge difference in perceived luxury. Offering Prosecco at breakfast, as commonly found in many European 5-star hotels, would also elevate the experience significantly. If the resort wants to compete in the “Champions League” of luxury hospitality, serving cordial drinks at breakfast should be reconsidered.

After we were told by the reception desk that our room wasn’t ready we gathered our belongings in the reception where we were immediately pounced on by the spa manager who handed each of us a treatment menu and stood over us while we looked at it. After we declined, we waited on sun loungers on the beach. There is a buzzer to the bar to order drinks - we buzzed and someone came after about 20 minutes. No urgency, definitely no luxury. Sitting by the pool wasn’t an option as there wasn’t anywhere inviting to sit. Even if there was, the loungers face into the main hotel restaurant (why?) and the pool is not nice to look at.

When our room was ready we went back through to reception - which was still chaotic and loud - we were loaded onto a buggy with other families and taken to our room. It felt more like a cattle lorry than a 5* resort buggy. The reception staff also informed us that we would need to turn on the hot water 10-15 minutes before using the shower, which was surprising for a resort of this alleged ‘quality’.

Upon entering our room we were hit by a really foul smell. There were hairs on the floor and in the sink, and stains on the pillows and bed sheets. We told the reception desk that we were going for lunch and requested that housekeeping return to the room.

We ate lunch at the Asean restaurant. We both ordered king prawn fried rice which arrived without the prawns and was clearly cooked in dirty old oil. This cost £25. We didn’t return. There were screens all around the restaurant and in reception advertising activities turtle hatching (which wasn’t really what I wanted to watch while eating) - very tacky.

We went back to our room which had been re-cleaned but still had a foul smell. Everything looks tired and dirty. We saw monkeys riffling through (clean) bed sheets and towels, so it’s no wonder. Our towels had brown marks on them and need replacing desperately. The water pressure in the room was terrible, and the air con units urgently require replacing (along with everything else). It’s hard to articulate but it really just felt like a budget hotel.

At this stage we informed the front desk that we would be checking out the following morning and we made new travel arrangements. They offered to upgrade our room but we had seen enough (I think we had booked the most superior room type anyway) so politely declined. We ate dinner at a restaurant just outside the resort called Aima Grill Fish Restaurant (unconnected to the hotel) which was far better than the food we ate at lunchtime. We skipped breakfast and left the next morning. We have never left a hotel early before. They offered to refund the second night - I’ll update this review if the refund doesn’t end up materialising.

Although the view from our room was nice, having been on the beach we had seen quite a lot of rubbish both in the sand and the sea. In particular we noticed that the staff who stand near the towel counter leave their cigarette butts in the sand (when there is a bin close by) which explains why they are all over the beach. There is also a problem with sand flies - other people were covered in bites and there were notices about the sand flies on the beach and in our room.

Everything is either old, tired, broken or a combination of these things. I’m not entirely sure where the money is spent (our 2N stay cost nearly RM5800) but it is most certainly not on the hotel, hygiene or the guest experience. It is so gross.

At best this is a 2* resort masquerading as a luxury hotel. It is a complete rip off and we will never return or recommend it to anyone.

Unfortunately, this was one of the most disappointing marine parks I’ve visited. We came here for snorkeling and an introductory dive expecting a beautiful, protected marine environment, but instead, large parts of the experience genuinely felt like swimming in a landfill.

There was an unbelievable amount of plastic and other waste both in the water and along the beach. While swimming, it was almost impossible not to encounter plastic bottles, bags, and other pieces of trash, sometimes even getting caught in your hair. I understand that currents can bring large amounts of waste into the area and that this is not necessarily something the park can prevent. However, what I cannot understand is how there seems to be so little organized effort to regularly remove it, especially from a place designated as a marine park and visited by tour boats every day. Everyone behaved as if this were completely normal and simply an everyday occurrence.

A French tourist family eventually took it upon themselves to start cleaning the beach and filled what looked like around 30 baskets with garbage. Seeing visitors taking responsibility for cleaning a marine park while people working there (mostly tour guides/divers)
carried on as normal was honestly quite shocking.

As for the marine life, we did see plenty of fish, which was nice, but unfortunately, most of the coral appeared to be dead or severely damaged. Considering this is a protected marine park, I expected a much healthier and more vibrant underwater ecosystem.

I really hope more is done to protect and maintain this place. If currents regularly bring this much waste here, then regular cleanups, collecting floating waste with nets, and better coordination with the tour operators visiting every day seem desperately needed. A marine park should be a place where marine ecosystems are actively protected, not somewhere visitors have to swim through plastic waste.

We had a great experience at Pulau Payar. I was a little hesitant to go because I couldn’t find a lot of recent reviews. But I’m glad we booked a trip here. I imagine it’s a much better experience now that they limit the number of visitors per day to 100. That being the case, you need to book ahead of time to make sure you get a spot. (Bookings open around 1 month prior to scheduled visit.)

We did the “Intro Dive” package, which includes an assisted 30 minute scuba dive, limited depth, followed by snorkeling. As we had never scuba dived before (and had no certification), this was perfect for us to try out scuba. We really enjoyed it and have a good idea now if we want to pursue certification or not. A master diver will stay with you the whole time. After the dive, we were able to snorkel the rest of the time. I found the visibility to be pretty good and there were some nice coral formations and a good variety of fish. We saw a lot of colorful fish (parrot fish and others), some squid, an eel, and a few puffer fish (some really big ones too!) to name a few highlights.

Our day looked like this:
Met at the Scuba Club at 8:30am to register, try on gear, etc. Got on the boat a little after 9am and took the 1 hr-long, fast, bumpy, wet ride to Pulau Payar. Because we were doing the intro dive, we were on a boat with other scuba divers, while another boat took snorkelers only. So I can’t really comment on what the snorkelers in the other boat did. We went to a site off of the main island and did our dive. Then we snorkeled around while the others continued their dives. We had lunch on the boat (simple chicken and rice dish), then went to another site. After the divers got off the boat in deeper water, then boat took us to the shallower water for us to snorkel. There was a beach there also where we could relax. But most of the time we stayed in the water. After an hour or so, we got back on the boat and headed back to Langkawi. We arrived back, changed clothes and turned in our wet suits.

There’s limited places to change clothes. Either you have to use a small bathroom or a storage closet area. But it’s essential you change into dry clothes if you’re looking to take a Grab from there. In fact, they told us to walk away from the Scuba Club a little ways before ordering the Grab, otherwise they won’t pick you up because they assume you are wet.

Shout out to Hello Langkawi and staff members Maui (Aoi) and Nasi. They took good care of us.

Overall Impression
Except for the view, everything else fell far below expectations. I paid nearly RM6,000 for 2 nights, but the stay was nowhere near worth the price. This is not a 5-star resort—it is closer to 3-star. The property relies solely on its location while neglecting service, facilities, and maintenance. Unfortunately, other guests have raised similar issues in past reviews, and it is clear that no real improvements have been made.

Ratings
•	Price/Value: 2/5
•	Scenery & Location: 4/5
•	Facilities: 2/5
•	Access: 2/5
•	Service Quality: 2/5
•	Dining: 1/5
•	Cleanliness: 3/5

Beach & Location
The white sand beach was beautiful, clean, and well maintained. The view from the Cliff Bayview Suite was stunning. On this point alone, the resort deserves 5/5.

Room & Facilities
The suite was poorly maintained: TVs did not work, the air conditioner was broken, the floors felt gritty, and the bed mattress was uncomfortably hard. Bathwater was yellowish and cloudy, and tap water had a strong unpleasant smell. In-room dining dishes were left in the hallway for over two days. The bathroom amenities (L’Occitane) had an overly strong, chemical scent.
There were also two large flies inside the room, which gave a very unclean.This did not feel like a 5-star resort.

Check-in / Check-out & Service
While early check-in was allowed, overall service was unfriendly and mechanical. The welcome drink was handed out carelessly. The check-in process was rushed, with no explanation of facilities or activities. At check-out, staff simply processed the paperwork with no smile, no feedback, and no hospitality.

Dining
Breakfast was poor: hot dishes were already cold, the selection was limited, and seasoning was extreme. Complimentary soft drinks were only high-sugar choices (Fanta, A&W, Coke). Overall, the food quality was closer to 3-star level.

Activities
The snorkeling tour was disappointing: many corals were bleached, fish variety was low, and the sea was overcrowded with tours from the nearby public beach.

Other Issues
Wi-Fi did not work. Hot water took over 15 minutes to arrive and quickly turned cold. Guests had to set up their own sun loungers and collect towels from the counter. No complimentary water was provided.

Access
The resort is difficult to reach: 1-hour flight from Kuala Lumpur to Kuala Terengganu, another 1-hour drive to the jetty, and then a 40-minute boat ride. For international travelers, it is a long journey with little reward.

All the staff members tried they absolute best to compensate for the lack of investment and maintenance from the Hotel owner.

Besides the staff the nature, land and sea is absolutely stunning. The beach is spotless and luckily plastic debris was not massive during our stay. This Resort could be an absolute jewel and probably was at the day of it’s opening in 1996.

And this is where the positive ends and the negative starts… the hotel and all amenities are screaming for a massive overhaul and renovation. It clearly appears that since the day of opening, no improvements have been made. We had to stop at one point to take pictures and document shortcomings not completely to get into a loop of doom and not seeing the beauty of having time as a family and enjoying the time and activities together (pictures attached).

To not lose your attention, please find bullet style the shortcomings of The Taaras
- trash below the balcony of the hotel room
- plastic-wrapped cheese at the breakfast buffet
- Room keys are still actual KEYS… and only 1 per room with a tag displaying the number of the room...
- not enough sun loungers for hotel guests, so you have to run out at 7:30 am in the morning to “reserve” your bench (like a cheap Costa del Sol Hotel)

Leave me in this paradise!

The hotel enjoys a spectacular location, surrounded by nature and overlooking the Redang Bay, a real corner of the world that looks painted. We stayed in a Cliff Bay suite, booked on Booking, which left us speechless: a huge and bright room, with private terrace and Jacuzzi seafront from which to admire sunrises and unforgettable sunsets. The comfortable bed, the spacious walk-in closet and the bathroom with Occitane products kit complete a well-kept environment in detail. The cleanliness was impeccable and every evening they made us find chocolates in the room, a simple but very refined thought that made us feel pampered.

To reach the suite, located in a panoramic position, it was enough to ask at the reception one of the electric machines that accompanied us comfortably up and down, a quick and efficient service that we found really practical.

The private beach is a real jewel: fine sand that seems borotalco, transparent sea and very comfortable beds. Any advice? Wake up early, around 7, to grab the first row and live the whole day with the bay in front, without any obstacle to the sight.

An experience that makes Redang unique in the world is the possibility to swim with adult marine turtles in their natural habitat and, at certain times, to witness the release of children directly from the beach: an emotion that will remain imprinted in the memory of children and adults. The snorkeling excursion in the nearby bay, populated by a myriad of colorful fish.

The breakfast was rich and varied, with international and local options. For meals we often stopped at The Cove, the bar-restaurant on the beach: relaxed atmosphere, tasty dishes and correct prices (a daisy or a hamburger about 12 €). Dining with the sea breeze and the sound of the waves in the background was an experience that alone was worth the trip.

The staff was always extremely kind and helpful, ready to meet every need with the smile, helping to make the stay even more enjoyable. a special thanks to the Hamdan referent who has always been attentive and helpful to give me advice and make us feel comfortable!

We spent four unforgettable nights, but the feeling, at the time of departure, was to not want to leave anymore. We stayed in August the weather was always perfect to enjoy the sea and outdoor activities.

What to say: money spent very well, a place that remains in the heart... I'd be back tomorrow!

I spent a wonderful stay at the Taras Resort in Redang, an experience that fully deserves 5 stars.

The thing I liked most was the private beach: quiet, cared for and with a spectacular sea.
Swimming, you can easily reach the Turtle Point and swim with turtles, a unique emotion.
The beds are well placed and the beach service is excellent: they bring you everything you want, creating an atmosphere of total relaxation.

Another highlight is the services included: yoga in the morning and in the afternoon, a wonderful gym with ocean views, kayaking, billiards, evening table tennis, karaoke room... also staying in the hotel for several days without hiking, there are many activities to never get bored.

The rooms are beautiful and comfortable. I recommend those with garden view or ocean view, which have the best position. Those with hill view require to take a transfer or make several stairs, so they are to be evaluated according to preferences and budget.

On the catering front, the hotel is mainly designed for an Asian audience, so the buffet is full of local dishes (very good: the roti and scramble eggs were excellent).
There is also a restaurant near the beach for dinner, good but not exceptional, and a wonderful seafront bar, where to eat burgers, pizza and drink with an amazing view.

Only sin for those who, like us, travel without children: there are many inflatables and games scattered for the hotel, so it happens to sip an aperitif with children jumping next door. It would be ideal to create an area dedicated only to children. The pools, often filled with children and guests who bathe clothes, are less enjoyable. In addition, the new building of rooms is somewhat ruining the landscape.

In summary: a resort with a postcard sea, plenty of activities and guaranteed relaxation, perfect for families and couples looking for services and comfort. Some improved details, but the overall experience was really beautiful

We stayed here for 3 days and 2 nights (Monday to Wednesday in July). A day before our arrival, we called the hotel to inform them of our ferry arrival time. On the day itself, we were warmly welcomed by the hotel’s shuttle van driver as soon as we arrived. At check-in, we were greeted by a cheerful receptionist and offered a refreshing welcome drink - perfect for the warm weather.

We checked into our Garden Suite shortly after. The room was clean, comfortable, and inviting. We quickly brewed the complimentary coffee capsules provided in the room to recharge before exploring the hotel grounds and heading to the beach.

The beach was stunning - clean with soft white sand and peaceful, as it wasn’t crowded during our stay. We tried kayaking for the first time, which turned out to be a fun and enlightening experience. The next morning, we joined the 8 AM guided nature walk - a nice bit of exercise, especially for those of us used to sitting behind a laptop. The guides were friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable throughout.

During our stay, we enjoyed breakfast at the Asean All-Day Dining restaurant on both mornings. The buffet spread had plenty of choices - enough to spoil any appetite. The atmosphere at the resort was lovely, and the staff were consistently cheerful and accommodating.

For those using Maxis/Hotlink, signal coverage is strong throughout the resort. I had planned to get some work done - but with a beach that tempting, it was impossible to resist relaxing instead.

The beautiful weather, powdery sand, and turquoise-blue sea felt almost surreal - like stepping into a painting. We also explored Turtle Beach, which is just a short walk from the resort’s private beach. It was a fun little adventure.

A big thank you to all the amazing staff here - the drivers, the receptionists, the lifeguards, the snorkeling guides, the room service team, and everyone else who made our stay so memorable.

We only wish the trip could have been longer. We’d definitely love to return!

7th to 13th of July 2025, What I appreciated most was the stunning white sandy beach and the spacious room with effortless beach access, which made things much easier while traveling with my one-year-old baby. A special mention goes to Hamdan, the room service assistant, whose kindness and attentiveness throughout my six-night stay at The Taaras truly stood out. The staff overall were warm and courteous, though I believe a touch more professional training would help meet the refined standards expected of a five-star resort. Among the dining experiences, both ASEAN and Merenero restaurant teams were welcoming, yet Merenero’s staff demonstrated a noticeably higher level of attentiveness. One memorable gesture was when I found myself without cash while waiting for the boat transfer—one of the staff not only guided me to the nearest ATM but personally took me there on his scooter, an act of genuine hospitality I won’t forget. On the less favorable side, the room furnishings felt outdated, with noticeable gaps that allowed lizards inside during my stay, and the towels were worn and rough on the skin. Breakfast lacked variety, leaving the experience feeling repetitive. Adding to that, aside from Hamdan, staff professionalism could be elevated; starting from Merang Jetty where I noticed staff smoking in the waiting area despite the presence of my baby, which felt far from appropriate. The same issue appeared at the scuba diving center, which is located right next to Merenero restaurant—I could even smell cigarette smoke while dining, something that diminished the overall experience. In summary, while I would gladly pay for the breathtaking beach alone, the overall cost—including flights, land and sea transfers, and the six-night stay—did not quite reflect the full value one might expect from such a resort.

Kapalai is located approximately 45 mins to 1 hour from Semporna town, via a speed boat. It provides a 360° breathtaking ocean view. We were amazed by the unpolluted turquoise sea water upon arrival. The water is clean and see-through to the sea bed.

Sea turtles were abundantly spotted around the resort. We were told by one of the buggy drivers that Kapalai has its own man-made beach to encourage the sea turtles to lay eggs. To date, Kapalai has managed to release more than 100 sea turtles into the ocean. Sipadan is famous for its Green and Hawksbill sea turtles.

While snorkelling, we spotted not only sea turtles but barracuda, colourful coral reefs, stingrays, starfishes, squids, to name a few. The snorkelling gear can be rented for RM23/day. The famous clear kayak boat can also be rented for RM50/hour. This is especially famous amongst the ladies. The staff of Kapalai are more than helpful to help you take the best photos of you riding on the kayak.

"Harley-Davidson" could be rented in the resort for RM50/day. Don't get me wrong, it is however not the real Harley-Davidson, mind the pun. The staff refers the pastel rattan coloured bicycle as Harley-Davidson. The bicycle complements the beautiful resort. Aplenty of photos could be taken with you riding on it too.

Due to the previous case of resort guests being kidnapped by the Philippines pirates, whom subsequently demanded hefty ransom from the Malaysian government, Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort is now safely and heavily guarded by the Royal Malaysian Navy.

I am writing this review to strongly warn other travelers.

I stayed three nights at the Perhentian Island Resort (Pulau Perhentian Besar, Turtle Beach). During my stay, I suffered clear and medically confirmed bedbug bites. The symptoms started after the first night and worsened each day, showing the typical linear pattern. A pharmacist confirmed this, and I have photo evidence.

What is even more alarming than the incident itself is how it was handled. After I reported the issue, I was moved to another room for the final hours before my departure. This was not a gesture of goodwill, but simply the minimum necessary response. At the same time, I was told that no responsible person was available to make any decisions regarding compensation and that I should follow up by email. I clearly stated already then that this approach would likely result in the issue being denied later. Unfortunately, this is exactly what happened.

After my departure, the resort refused to take responsibility, claiming no evidence was found. I find it unacceptable that such a serious issue is being dismissed despite clear documentation.

In addition, I had significant effort and costs: medication, disinfection of luggage and rental car, and repeated laundry cycles — all during an ongoing international trip.

However, the core issue goes far beyond this single incident. This resort shows fundamental and systemic problems:
- Serious hygiene deficiencies (e.g. insects all over buffet food areas)
- Passive and disengaged staff despite high staff presence
- Lack of even basic safety standards

During a snorkeling trip, guests were not checked for their ability to swim. This led to two guests nearly drowning — they had to be rescued by myself and another tourist, not by the staff. I was personally involved and can fully confirm this.

These are not isolated failures. They indicate deep and ongoing mismanagement. Issues like bedbugs do not occur randomly — they are a consequence of sustained neglect.

Yes, the location is beautiful. But this does not justify risks to health and safety.

I strongly and explicitly advise anyone against staying at this resort.

I still expect appropriate compensation. If the resort continues to deny responsibility, I will proceed with legal action and involve the relevant authorities.

Avoid this resort!
