KAPALAI DESERVES MORE!

We stayed 6 nights and 7 days at this fantastic resort. I would like to share my experience so that those who choose this resort are aware of the significant limitations that unfortunately this magnificent structure presents.

Value for money 5/10
Considering a cost of about 650 euros per night for two people (High season - diving package with 3 or 4 dives per day), I wouldn't return to this resort.

The company policy is mainly oriented on the Asian market, and this choice affects numerous aspects that I will list here:

1. The transfer by speedboat from Semporna Port to Kapalai was not at all comfortable. We are used to the sea, and I understand that the weather conditions cannot be controlled, and there is an internal schedule to follow. However, I would like to emphasize that the boat was not suitable for those sea conditions; the rigid hull continuously slammed against the waves, resulting in a sore back. The captain could have easily reduced the speed.

2. Inadequate and unprepared staff. The management was careless in addressing various issues raised, and there was a total lack of authority in enforcing the necessary rules for civil coexistence and respect for this magnificent ecosystem and for those who wanted to spend relaxing moments.

2. Hygiene, cleanliness, and maintenance of the structure need improvement. The rooms are large and spacious with air conditioning, a fan, kettle, minibar, and safe, but a bit outdated. Maintenance is needed, especially in the bathroom. There are different types of chalets, some recently renovated. At the time of check-in, the room was very dirty, the wooden floor had not been cleaned, dust everywhere, especially on the shelves of the open wardrobe, and we even found a used soap in the shower. Towels were washed and fragrant but stained (despite being changed every day). Bird droppings on the balcony were not cleaned for days. Periodically, between 1:00 PM and 5:00 PM, maintenance workers start their work, and they don't care about the noise they make. The wooden planks of the pier that connect the rooms, since they are not properly fixed, make a terrible noise every time bicycles or golf carts pass near the room (this happens at all hours).

3. Environmental awareness and pollution control are non-existent. The showers in the rooms drain directly into the fantastic crystalline waters surrounding the resort, releasing polluting substances from the used soaps and organic waste (we even saw floating organic waste). Some areas of the resort's walkways are cleaned with bleach, which ends up directly in the sea after washing/rinsing.

4.Non-existent internet connection (this could be a plus for some). Wi-Fi is only available in the reception area, but it's very slow. Despite buying local SIM cards for data connection, the signal was completely absent for 2 days due to issues with the resort's receiver antenna
.
5. Good food for those who enjoy Asian cuisine. There is a total absence of continental dishes, only predominantly Asian cuisine with limited variety

The location and the beach in front of the hotel are, without a doubt, THE BEST ON THE ISLAND — that's the positive part. The negatives:

1- The hotel restaurant needs a lot of improvement. Prices are a bit higher than in other areas, which would be fine if the food were good, but it isn't (except for a few specific dishes). You can tell no one's really keeping an eye on things, no manager supervising. Breakfast is basic but fine.

2- The rooms are THE WORST PART — maintenance is basically NONEXISTENT. Walls, closets, floors — everything is worn out and old. If that were all, the rating would be higher, but no — CLEANLINESS NEEDS TO BE IMPLEMENTED. There are no mosquito nets on the beds; last night we had to kill, without exaggeration, 15 tiny insects I couldn't identify, they looked like mini-mosquitoes. Given that we always kept everything closed and shut the door right away, I understand you're in the jungle and there will be bugs, but not in that quantity — they need to put measures in place so this doesn't happen. We paid €113 per night (for a standard room, not near the sea), not €30. And what really left us speechless was finding a large amount of some kind of sandy grit under the bed — after looking into it a bit, it seems to be termite droppings, I'm NOT SURE, but it definitely wasn't sand. In conclusion, you don't sleep comfortably.

3- The service: it's true we met some pleasant people, but there were others who weren't particularly friendly.

I don't know if this is an isolated situation or not, since we haven't stayed at other hotels on this island — I don't know how common it is, but we stayed at Ombak Resort (on Kecil) and it was much better, both the restaurant, the rooms, and the service.

The beach is paradise, but the resort is hell.

After a long journey, our first experience at another place, Fauna Beach Resort, was so miserable and poorly maintained that we immediately started looking for an alternative. Thankfully, for a bit more money, we were able to book a stay at Perhentian Island Resort, and it turned out to be the best decision we made on our entire long vacation.

You have to remember that this is an island, and everything has to be brought in by boat, which makes the level of care and cleanliness at this resort truly remarkable. There are no highways, landfills, or hardware stores, yet they manage to keep everything in pristine condition.

The last resort|Unfortunately, I whole-heartedly agree with previous reviewers. There are only two factors that keep the resort going - the wonderful beach and sea access, and the fact that - at least during the current high season - the demand for rooms is such that even very over-rated (and over-paid) facilities like the PIR get filled.  It sort of becomes the 'last resort' for people like us who do not book super-early and so miss out on any of the chain of much better places (supposedly lower grade) on this larger of the two islands - including Coral View, Abdul's Chalet, Mama's, Tuna Bay and several others.  All markedly better in most respects than the Perhentian Island Resort.  The place visibly dates back to the 80s, and much of it has not been renovated / updated since then.  No need to repeat what others have said - but just a few examples of the many seemingly little things that 'irked' us.  Breakfast - buffet type, but with low quality products throughout - old (non-fresh) chewy 'croissants', low quality juices, really almost undrinkable coffee... large round tables with unironed table-cloth that still have food remnants from the night before.  No ROTI CANAI - which is a major product produced and consumed for breakfast at the other, smaller resorts. Service people stand in corners of the room but are not helpful at all (except when collecting the pointless breakfast vouchers..).  There is an espresso / coffee machine - but when you ask, any 'good coffee' costs extra (different from 4 star hotels elsewhere).  - Rooms: no hot water (not essential here, but nice to have - available in some of the 'lower grade' resorts nearby).  No TV (again, not essential - but the others have it). Rooms all need to be 'redone' as well as thoroughly cleaned. - Staff - many are friendly and helpful enough, but generally do not seem to be trained well, or speak enough English for this kind of place.  Management / supervision overall seems to be lacking.  Example: we finally moved out to another resort.  The front desk is asked to call the other resort to send a boat. Staff tries once to call, then turns to us and says: no one answering the phone.  We try and immediately get someone and so arrange it all ourselves. - Anyway - our bottom line, and recommendation would be for the owners to do 2 main things: 1) to close the entire place for an entire season (or whatever it takes) to do a major overhaul of the entire facility, and 2) equally important, to seriously strengthen management and supervision, as well as retrain staff.

我们于2025年7月25日（星期五）上午11:45抵达大停泊岛，但并无酒店员工迎接或指引。我们自行拖行李前往接待处后才得知酒店其实有行李运送服务，但并未在码头提供协助，实在不合理。

办理入住后被告知下午三点才能拿房，而我们的三天两夜浮潜配套第一场活动是在当天下午三点。多数酒店通常会弹性安排提前入住以配合行程，但这家酒店没有任何协调，只让我们寄存贵重物品。

浮潜结束后回到酒店，却发现行李被随意放在房门口。询问之下，工作人员称“不能随意进房”，但行李却能丢在无人看管的走廊两小时，无闭路电视保障，安全隐患极大。

入住后还发现冰箱里有半瓶喝过的水，明显房间未彻底清洁。而第二天虽然我们挂了“请勿打扰”牌子，外出浮潜回来后却发现有人进入更换了毛巾和水，前后政策矛盾。

泳池也未清洁彻底，底部明显布满污垢，令人却步。此外，酒店物价离谱，一罐普通汽水竟要RM9，远高于一般岛上酒店。

尽管大停泊岛本身风景迷人，我未来可能还会再来，但绝不会再入住这家酒店，服务水平与价格严重不符。

We arrived at Perhentian Besar Island at 11:45 AM on July 25, 2025, but no hotel staff were present to greet or assist us. We had to carry our luggage ourselves to reception, only to find out later that luggage service was supposed to be provided—why wasn’t anyone at the jetty?

After checking in, we were told we could only access our room at 3 PM, even though our snorkeling package likely had the first session at 2 PM. Other hotels typically allow early check-in for such cases, but no flexibility was offered here.

The experience was awful from the very beginning. Cleanliness was virtually nonexistent, both in the rooms and in the common areas. In the room, only the towels were changed (and they were old, torn, and stained), but the floor was never swept or mopped, and the bathroom was not cleaned. I had to repeatedly ask for basic supplies like toilet paper and soap. The mattress was extremely hard, making it impossible to rest properly. I reported it, but received no reply or willingness to solve the issue.
Housekeeping knocked on the door at 8 a.m. every day, regardless of whether guests wanted to rest a little longer. On top of that, there were scheduled power outages every morning and afternoon, which turned off the air conditioning and often disabled the hot water system — which already worked poorly via a button that sometimes didn’t respond at all.

Breakfast was extremely basic and unhygienic. The cheese was cheap, pre-packaged, and cut in half; the utensils were poorly washed; nothing was ever restocked. The dining area was dirty and clearly neglected, with spills, used plates, and a complete lack of organization.
The hotel is in visible disrepair: broken tiles patched with cement, rusty fixtures, litter in the garden, deteriorated furniture, and no visible maintenance of any kind.

The staff was unfriendly and uninterested. They never smiled or greeted guests, and acted like everything was a bother. I made several complaints — both in person and via WhatsApp, which is the only way to reach them — and none were ever answered. There is no phone in the room, and there is no Wi-Fi outside of the reception area, which is also not clearly stated when booking. Guests are given no information about the hotel or the island, and communication is practically nonexistent. If you have an urgent issue, good luck — no one responds.

The natural beauty of the location is the only positive thing, but that is not thanks to the hotel. The way this place is run is a total disgrace. I would strongly advise against staying here.
